security_spec.violation_condition: The Linux kernel boots on a RISC-V hardware implementation that does not provide M-mode (violating the normative mmode_req rule), causing the kernel in S-mode/HS-mode to be the de facto highest privilege level with no higher authority to enforce PMP, delegate traps, gate CSR access, or provide SBI services.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: arch/riscv/ arch/riscv/kernel/ SBI_ECALL sbi_ecall mcounteren mstateen medeleg mideleg PMP pmp riscv_pmp satp_mode mstatus.TVM __sbi_ecall
security_spec.summary: M-mode is the mandatory highest privilege level with unfettered machine access; the kernel depends on M-mode for trap delegation, physical memory protection, CSR access gating, and SBI services — its absence collapses all privilege boundaries.
